_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 5: VLT / MUSE (WFM) and Keck II / KCWI (blue BM + Medium, blue BL + Large, red KCRM RL + Medium)
_meta.companion: data/round5/muse_kcwi.md (same content as Markdown sections in the format of data/presets_research.md); same JSON structure as data/presets_sources_3.json and data/round4/*.json. Extra keys: recommended_presets_by_mode (MUSE) / recommended_presets_by_config (KCWI) with explorer inputs as numbers; is_derived on values that are themselves arithmetic; stage on design-phase values; multiplex holds the objects-per-exposure rows.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (is_derived = the value itself is derived). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). EFFECTIVE = a value DERIVED to make the explorer reproduce published performance where the prescription is not published. Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Quotes copied from pdftotext (layout and raw) / tag-stripped HTML / raw repository text; compared with all whitespace removed, case-folded, with double/single primes, curly quotes, ˝, dashes, minus, micro/mu, ×, tilde-operator glyphs normalised and hyphens (incl. line-end hyphenation) ignored; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells. Text-layer renderings kept as rendered where noted (M18 "0.3500" = 0.35", "4000" = 40"; W20 "100. 705" = 1".705).

muse.title: VLT (UT4) / MUSE, Wide Field Mode (image-slicer IFU: 24 identical IFUs, each = 48-slice image slicer + refractive VPH spectrograph + 4k x 4k CCD)
muse.recommended_preset: One preset (WFM, nominal; all 24 IFUs identical, no moving parts). Sourced: D = 8.2 m (VLT UT4; focal-plane scale 1.705"/mm, i.e. f/14.75 on 8.2 m); slice width 0.2" (the "slit"); 48 slices per IFU (4 stacks of 12, each slice 15" x 0.2", ~75 px long on the CCD) = 3600 spaxels per detector; anamorphic fore-optics (x2 across the slices), so one 0.2" spaxel lands on 15 um (1 px) along the slice and 30 um (2 px) along the dispersion; camera f/1.95 (spatial direction); collimator = Lens (fully refractive); one VPH grating (KOSI) in first order; e2v 4096 (X) x 4112 (Y) x 15 um, dispersion along Y (Nx = 4112, Ny = 4096). NOT published: collimator and camera focal lengths, beam size, VPH line density and angle. EFFECTIVE values are DERIVED (not a prescription): f_cam = 258.4 mm and f_col = 499.3 mm from the MUSE-derived Potsdam MRS spectrograph (MRS16), W = 68.5 mm in the dispersion plane (so that the 0.2" slice is 2.0 px wide; spatial-direction pupil 133-137 mm), F = f_col / W = 7.29 (dispersion plane; 3.65-3.77 in the spatial direction), VPH G = 458.4 /mm at the symmetric Bragg setting alpha = beta = 9.23 deg for lamC = 7000 A (only G x f_cam / cos(beta) = 1.2e5 is fixed by the 1.25 A/px dispersion). Validate against: 1.25 A/px (MUM; 1.19-1.31 A/px across the range, W20); R = 1609 / 2737 / 3506 at 4650 / 7000 / 9350 A (MUM lab table); 2.5 px per resolution element (MUM); LSF FWHM 3.0 A at the blue end to 2.4 A at 7500 A (B17); fully sampled range 4750-9350 A nominal, 4600(4650)-9350 A extended (W20, MUM); 0.2"/px along the slices (MUM).

Cross-check: a 4096 x 15 um detector maps back to 61.44/0.5175 = 118.7 mm of slit, the MRS "up to 118 mm" input slit, consistent with an unchanged collimator/camera pair. conflicts: Detector: "E2V Deep depletion" 4096 x 4112 (MUM Table 3) vs "24 x 4k x 4k MIT/LL CCD" (ESOMO table).
Resolving power: 1770 (480 nm) - 3590 (930 nm) (MUM Table 1, ESOMO) vs 1770 at 465 nm - 3590 at 930 nm (ESOMI) vs lab table 1609 (465 nm) - 3506 (935 nm) (MUM Sec. 3.2) vs "R ~ 3000" (W20).
Camera focal ratio: f/1.95 (L10A abstract) vs F/1.9 (J20) vs f/1.89 (8.2 m) or f/1.93 (8.0 m) DERIVED from 15 um per 0.2".
Anamorphoser axis: "0.5 ... in the horizontal direction" (MUM) vs "2 ... in the vertical direction" (ESOMI); same 2:1 ratio.
Spectra per IFU: 48 x 75 = 3600 (DERIVED from MUM) vs 3750 on the first IFU (B10) vs 300 x 300 / 24 = 3750 (B06 field and sampling).
Spaxel size along the slices at the slicer: 465 um (MUM) vs 89.5 mm/300 spaxels x 1.51 = 450 um (DERIVED from L14).
Coverage: 4750-9350 A fully sampled (W20 Sec. 3.6, B17) vs at least 4800-9300 A (W20 Sec. 1.2) vs 480-930 nm (MUM); extended 4600 (W20 Sec. 3.6) vs 4650 A (W20 Sec. 1.2; MUM 465 nm).
notes: Explorer mapping: the explorer has one isotropic magnification, but MUSE is anamorphic (A = 2). The preset is set up for the DISPERSION plane (slit width 0.2" -> 2.0 px, W = 68.5 mm, F = 7.29), which fixes R, A/px and coverage. Its along-slit pixel scale then reads 0.10"/px; the real along-slice scale is 0.2"/px because the pupil is twice as wide (133-137 mm, camera f/1.89-1.95) in the spatial direction. Equivalently, the spatial direction behaves as F = 3.65-3.77.

Only G x f_cam / cos(beta) is constrained (1.2e5, from 1.25 A/px with 15 um pixels): any f_cam gives the same A/px, coverage and R if G is scaled as 1/f_cam; only the drawn angles change (alpha ~ 9 deg at f_cam = 258 mm).
MUSE uses a flat, tilted detector to absorb axial colour (B06); the explorer has a flat untilted focal plane.
R from the explorer is geometric (slit-limited, 2.0 px); the measured LSF (2.4-3.0 A, ~2.5 px) includes optics and detector blur, so the explorer over-predicts R by ~2-17% (largest in the blue).
NFM (0.025"/px, 7.42" x 7.43") uses the same spectrographs with x8 extra magnification in the fore-optics (ESOMI); the spectral format is identical (MUM).

notes: KCWI has no anamorphic fore-optics: the reflective slicer sits at the f/13.7 telescope focus and the collimator (f = 2172.5 mm) is filled by the 160 mm compound pupil (f/13.6), so one isotropic explorer magnification is correct (both the slice width and the along-slice scale come out right with D = 10.95 m, F = 13.7, W = 160 mm, f_cam = 304.4 mm).
The explorer slit for an IFU = one slice; "number of spectra" = 24 slices (or 3330 spatial pixels at 1x1, ~1665 at 2x2 binning).

Grating mode: transmission VPH with a fixed incidence (tAlpha) and the camera following beta; the camera articulation angle = alpha + beta. Blue typical alpha: BL 15, BM 30, BH 50-55 deg (M18 Table 2), with beta ~ alpha - 9 deg at the design central wavelength because of the ~2 deg fringe tilt.
The virtual slit is curved in 3-D ("C"-shaped) and the pipeline uses a 4 deg mean out-of-plane diffraction angle; the explorer works in plane (0.24% in lambda).
KCRM shares the slicer, collimator and FM1 with the blue arm; a 560 nm dichroic takes the place of the FMD fold mirror (KSPEC, KPRIM, M18 Fig. 2 caption).
